**The blocker in one line.** On a quiet machine, `PLAT_TIMING_TOKEN=<t> corepack pnpm bench:timing-phase` refuses
itself with `contended-machine`. The two processes it names are its own launch chain:
- the `corepack pnpm` node process, an ancestor, at 12–14 % CPU;
- the tsx esbuild service, a child of the script's own process, at 75–78 % CPU.

The preflight samples the machine at start-up, with no idle wait. This is CONFIRMED in 3 of 3 runs in the mirror. A
30 s idle before the preflight clears it (also CONFIRMED). This is a refusal of a lawful state, so it falls under
ZERO REFUSALS and N-58, and the verdict is MAKE-IT-SUCCEED. Details are under B1 below.

**The new class this check finds is B1.** `contended-machine` is reached from a **LAWFUL** state: an idle machine
running only the script's own launch. Verdict MAKE-IT-SUCCEED. The refusal's alternative ("stop the processes named")
cannot be followed, because the processes named are the script's own launch chain.

A further reach of the same class is lawful by design and is not a finding. The first act refuses after three
non-authoritative attempts. On this Linux host it always would, because `pmset` gives no AC reading. That is an
UNLAWFUL state for §12.1's timing phase: this is not the reference machine.

### BLOCKERS

**B1 — the script refuses its own start on a quiet machine (a refusal of a lawful state; the real path of the
interface `corepack pnpm bench:timing-phase` with `PLAT_TIMING_TOKEN`).**

`timingPhase` (`bench/src/timing-phase/index.ts:289–301`) runs the preflight as the very first thing after the token
check:

```
detect({ ownPids: [], checkLoad: false })
```

It refuses on any offender, with no idle wait. M0-f-01's detector (C-0138) exempts the launch chain and the tsx esbuild
child from the kind clause only. At ≥ 10 % CPU they still contend. Its `ownTree` counts this process's children only
when they are listed. Right after start-up, both are hot.

Evidence, CONFIRMED, from the mirror on this otherwise idle container. `ps` showed only `process_api`, the telemetry
collector, the environment manager and `claude` at 3.2 %.

```
$ PLAT_TIMING_TOKEN=checker-probe-1 corepack pnpm bench:timing-phase -- --only streamKey      → exit 3
timing-phase: REFUSE (contended-machine): timing-phase: the detector names 2 other process(es) on the machine (C-0103): MainThread (pid 6951, 11.5 % CPU); esbuild (pid 6988, 76.4 % CPU)
```

A second run gave `MainThread (pid 7068, 13.8 % CPU); esbuild (pid 7129, 75.5 % CPU)`. `ps` snapshots taken through
that run identify them:

```
7068  7067 13.8  MainThread  node /root/.local/bin/corepack pnpm bench:timing-phase -- --only streamKey   (an ancestor)
7115  7099 76.6  MainThread  /opt/node24/bin/node --require …/tsx/dist/preflight.cjs …                    (the script itself)
7129  7115 77.0  esbuild     …/@esbuild/linux-x64/bin/esbuild --service=0.28 …                            (a child of the script)
```

A third run with a probe patch in the mirror printed the offenders. The patch was restored byte-identical, checked with
`cmp`:

```
no idle:          PROBE preflight offenders: [["MainThread",7475,12.4,"cpu"],["esbuild",7512,77.5,"cpu"]]
after 30 s idle:  PROBE preflight offenders: []
```

On the owner's Mac this is PLAUSIBLE. macOS `ps -o pcpu` is a decaying recent-CPU average, and the preflight runs
within a second or two of esbuild's start-up transpile of the bench and packages sources.

The script's tests cannot see this:
- "a quiet machine … runs" plants a reading holding only this process;
- "a real python3 child … REFUSE naming its pid" checks only that python3 is *among* the reasons, so it passes whether
  or not the launch chain is also named.

The brief's (3) requires the detector's process census to work on both hosts. ZERO REFUSALS requires that a lawful state
never be refused.

**Required change** (a fix round of M0-t-00, in its owns only; M0-f-01's detector stays unchanged):
- Make the preflight succeed on a quiet machine running only the script's own launch. For example, take it after the
  protocol's 30 s idle (`IDLE_MS`, through the `sleep` seam), as every `timeBatch` and the first act already do. Any
  other rule the fixer prefers must be stated in an amended C-0440 (10)/(12) clause, never by widening another item's
  file.
- Keep a planted `python3` or Chromium outside the tree refused after the idle.
- Add a test that fails on today's code. Example: a planted reading sequence whose start-up sample holds an ancestor
  `node` at ≥ 10 % CPU and an `esbuild` child of this process at ≥ 10 % CPU, and whose post-idle sample is quiet. The
  test must show the script runs and that the preflight's reading was taken after the idle. Also tighten the
  real-detector test so it asserts which offenders it names.
- Re-run the real command in a mirror with a token: it must get past the preflight.

holding only pnpm state) and two logs in `/home/user/`. I identified them by their 23:39:10 timestamps and generated
contents, and removed them at once. No `plat/` file and no tracked root file changed. To find them I listed the project
root's top level (`ls -la`) once. I opened nothing under any clean-room-closed folder. This is disclosed in L-0684.
